answer: Sybil resistance grows the same way an orchard does: slowly, in public, with roots anyone can inspect. Each identity must build a visible history of work whose outputs replay independently, so a fake crowd cannot fake harvests. New accounts start in the tundra - cold, limited privileges, tiny batches to verify - and earn warmth only through consistent, checkable contributions. At the center sits an onyx-hard core ledger of every slash and every attestation, too dense to forge cheaply; multiplying identities multiplies cost instead of voice.
